text: {"rules":[{"jurisdiction":"CA","level":"state","category":"security_deposits","status":"in_force","title":"California security deposit cap and return rules (AB 12)","requirement":"Starting July 1, 2024, landlords may generally charge a security deposit of no more than one month's rent, for both furnished and unfurnished units. Landlords who own only two rental properties with no more than four residential units total may charge up to two months' rent if ownership is held by a natural person, family trust, or LLC whose members are all natural persons. Last month's rent counts as part of the deposit; first month's rent does not. Any remaining deposit must be returned within 21 days after the tenant vacates, with an itemized statement and supporting documents if deductions are made. Deductions are limited to unpaid rent, damage beyond normal wear and tear, cleaning to the move-in level, and (if the lease allows) restoring or replacing personal property. Other requirements: a unit walk-through inspection offered in the last two weeks of the tenancy; photographs of the unit at the start of tenancies beginning on or after 2025-07-01; proof of completed repairs from 2025-01-01; and post-tenancy photographs before repairs or cleaning from 2025-04-01.","key_value":"1 month's rent (2 months for small natural-person/LLC owners with at most 2 properties and 4 units); return within 21 days","coverage_conditions":"Residential rentals statewide.
